newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: EUTHANASIA DEBATE TO CONTINUE
The euthanasia debate continues today....with Federal politicians examining whether the Northern Territory's euthanasia laws should stand.
Liberal back-bencher Kevin Andrews has put forward a private members bill to over-ride the NT laws.
Members are voting according to their conscience, rather than on party lines - a process which has divided both major parties.
Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone says the Territory's Country Liberal Party and its two federal M-P's are unhappy with the way they've been treated by their Federal partners.
Sixty speakers are scheduled to continue the debate on Thursday, following a failed bid to refer the issue to a committee.
NITSCHKE SAYS MANY GIVING UP HOPE OF USING EUTHANASIA LAW

The doctor who helped Darwin man Bob Dent become the first person use the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law, says some people waiting to use the law have given up hope, as legal and political obstacles abound.
Dr Philip Nitschke says he knows of about ten more people, mostly from interstate, who want to use the law.
But Dr Nitschke says many fear the Federal debate will overturn the legislation, or that voluntary euthanasia will be restricted to Territorians.
TROUBLEMAKERS IN ALICE SPRINGS
It's claimed aborigines visiting Alice Springs have no respect for either sacred sites or European laws.
Aboriginal elders say some Aborigines from bush communities are coming into the Alice, and fighting, drinking and causing problems between families.
President of the Four Corners elders' council Eli Rubuntja says the troublemaking attitude is causing a serious problem for the all the people of the Alice.
THE SEARCH IS ON FOR ELIGIBLE WALLABIES
Male Brush-tailed rock wallabies continue to be the most elusive bachelors in Victoria's East Gippsland.
While four prospective brides pine away in the Healesville sanctuary, the remaining males of the rare wallaby remain unwilling to enter the wildlife traps that could lead to matrimony.
It's thought there are fewer than forty Bush Tailed Rock Wallabies still living in the Snowy River area, and wildlife officers are anxious to start a captive breeding programme.
PILOT'S SKILL SAVES LIVES
An inquiry into the June Blackhawk disaster near Townsville has been told the survivors on Blackhawk Two, owe their lives to the skill of their pilot.
The Military Board inquiry, investigating the mid air collision which killed 18 soldiers, heard they'd survived because they were in a Blackhawk helicopter and because of the skill of Captain Burke.
On Blackhawk Two, Loadmaster Sergeant William Mark had called "come right" to his pilot.. and then "come up" when the aircraft were still converging.
Co-pilot Lieutenant Simon Edwards and Sergeant Mark said the blades hit and they went into a spin.
Both recall pilot Captain Burke saying we're dead.
AUSTRALIA'S HOMELESS ON THE INCREASE
More Australians are literally being forced onto the streets because they can't afford to keep a roof over their heads.
Melbourne Welfare agency, Hanover Welfare, says there's been a marked increase in the number of people living in squats, sleeping out in the open, or in over-crowded situations.
Hanover Chief Executive Tony Nicholson says the agency has found a doubling in the number of people evicted from the private rental market in the past four years.
In the past two years, there's been a five percent jump in the number of clients sleeping out or using squats.
THREE STRIKES AGAINST CHANNEL NINE'S PROGRAMMING
The Australian Broadcasting Authority has found TCN Channel Nine failed to comply with program standards on three occasions over the past three years.

TCN failed to comply with the minimum Australian drama requirement last year, the minimum three-year drama score between 1993 and 1995 and the requirement for broadcasting "C" classified children's programs in 1994.
An ABA spokesman says TCN claims its failure to meet the Australian drama requirement was due to the incorrect assumption that the Paul Hogan film "Almost an Angel" was an Australian drama.
FORMER AUSTRALIAN RUGBY REPRESENTATIVE DIES
Former Australian under-19 rugby player Ian Tucker has died after suffering a head injury while playing for Oxford University on the weekend.
Tucker had been on a life support machine since being injured in a first division match on Saturday.
The 23-year-old played for Australia against New Zealand four years ago..and represented New South Wales at under-17, 19, and 21 levels.
WINDS SLOW DOWN SOLAR CHALLENGERS
Leading entrants in the World Solar Challenge will be heading for the South Australian border this morning.
But organiser say gusty winds are expected to slow down competitors again today.
The Japanese Honda car, which is leading the Darwin to Adelaide race at the half-way mark, averaged nearly 90-kilometres an hour yesterday, with winds reaching 30 knots at times.
Schooler, the Swiss entry, is second, averaging a speed of 83 kilometres an hour.
TOP LINEUP FOR HOPMAN CUP
Hopman Cup organisers say this year's line-up is the most powerful in its nine year history ... but the event's only guaranteed in Perth for three years.
Tournament director Paul MacNamee says International Tennis
Federation recognition means the I-T-F may decide within five years to shift the event.
But he says the new status from tennis' ruling body has helped attract a "star-studded field" including Steffi Graf, Mary Pierce, Goran Ivanisevic and Mark Phillippousis.
NO HOLIDAY FOR 3000 HOLIDAYMAKERS
It's thought up to three-thousand holidaymakers have been caught out by the collapse of three companies offering Gold Coast holidays.
The would-be holidaymakers have been locked out the accommodation they'd reserved through the companies, which have folded after running into financial difficulties.
The Department of Consumer Affairs is investigating the complaints as a matter of priority and has set up a special information hotline for distressed tourists.
ATHLETES MAY BE BETTER OFF WITH HIGH FAT DIET
A Canberra conference will today hear that some athletes could gain the edge over their competitors by changing to a high-fat diet just before they compete.
South African sports physiologist John Hawley will outline his research at the Australian Conference of Science and Medicine in Sport.

Dr Hawley says that top performance in some athletic events may be easier to achieve if an athlete trains for most of the year on a moderate carbohydrate diet, then changes to a high fat diet before competing.
He says it could be of particular benefit to endurance athletes.
AUSTRALIAN SQUASH PLAYER BEATS JANSHER KHAN
Australian squash player Craig Rowland has scored a sensational victory over world champion Jansher Khan at the Tournament of Champions in New York.
The unseeded Rowland won in straight games to advance to the final against Canadian Jonathon Power.
